subject.title: fix(diagnostics): prune non-idle ghost entries after failed stuck-session recovery

question: Should failed-recovery ghosts be made prune-eligible through the recovery coordinator’s ownership checks, or is a broader time-based diagnostic-state eviction an accepted product contract?
rationale: The correct boundary determines whether this PR may remove state that a live recovery path still owns; the closed related proposal is design evidence but is not a landing-ready replacement.

options.title: Require ownership-aware cleanup
options.body: Move the repair to the failed-recovery path or add equivalent owner and queue checks before a non-idle entry becomes prune-eligible.

options.title: Accept bounded diagnostic eviction
options.body: Accept the 90-minute age-only fallback as intentional and document that diagnostic state may be discarded even if the session has not emitted activity.

options.title: Pause for a narrower replacement
options.body: Close or pause this branch if maintainers prefer a focused recovery-coordinator fix rather than changing global prune semantics.

recommendation.title: Require ownership-aware cleanup
recommendation.body: Move the repair to the failed-recovery path or add equivalent owner and queue checks before a non-idle entry becomes prune-eligible.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report contains the clearest source-level account of the failed-recovery invariant that needs an owner decision.
